Right: three nodes in an undirected graph (named in the accent note above it); a triad must be directed, so is_triad() returns False." width="100%"} ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` for a directed graph with exactly three nodes and no self-loops. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Matches NetworkX's `is_triad`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#c8256fef .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]).add_edge("A", "B") g.is_triad(), ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]).is_triad() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
